solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cut price of fine material? (8)

blocks.note: lace is a fine, delicate fabric
a rate is a price, as in 'the going rate'

annotation.surface: A shopper asks whether the price of a delicate fabric has been slashed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut price' reads as one phrase, a bargain; split it, and 'Cut' is the definition while 'price' starts the wordplay. 'Of' lets the price belong to the material, which fixes the order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacerate is the medical word for cutting or tearing skin.

entries.clue: Property recipient once called in support of first-class story (7)

indicatorNotes.in support of: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so NEE comes after A + LIE

blocks.note: A is the top grade
a story can be a fib
née gives a woman's name before marriage

annotation.surface: A former name props up a top-class tale about who got the property.
annotation.walkthrough: An alienee is a legal term: the person property is transferred (alienated) to. 'Once called' is née, as in 'Mrs Smith, née Jones'.
annotation.definitionFit: In law, an alienee is the person to whom property is alienated, or transferred.

entries.clue: Charmingly wind up lady on vacation transfixed by heartless stud? (11)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: LADY is vacated, or emptied, of its middle letters, leaving L and Y
indicatorNotes.transfixed by: END + LY is pierced by EARING, which goes inside
indicatorNotes.heartless: EARRING loses its heart, the middle R

blocks.note: to wind up is to end
a stud is an EARRING; take out the middle R
LADY with its inside removed

annotation.surface: Someone playfully teases a woman who is going on holiday about her stud earrings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' pretends to mean tease, and 'stud' pretends to be a man. A stud here is an earring, and the earring 'transfixes' END + LY the way a stud goes through an ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something endearingly means doing it in a charming, lovable way.

entries.clue: Old author brought up main work (5)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing SEA up turns it around, giving AES

blocks.note: the main is the open sea
OP is short for opus, a work

annotation.surface: A writer from the past raises the subject of his chief book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main work' wants to be a single phrase, a masterpiece. Split, 'main' is the poets' word for the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the fables.

entries.clue: Chosen Republican American, one with daddy issues? (7)

blocks.note: elect means chosen, as in 'the president-elect'
R = Republican
A = American

annotation.surface: A US politician who has just been voted in turns out to have a complicated relationship with their father.
annotation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Electra helped avenge her father Agamemnon. Jung named the Electra complex after her: a daughter's fixation on her father.
annotation.definitionFit: Electra gives her name to the Electra complex, a daughter's obsessive attachment to her father.

entries.clue: Shame about your abstention from sex (6)

indicatorNotes.about: PITY goes about, or around, UR

blocks.note: 'what a shame' = 'what a pity'
UR is text-speak for 'your'

annotation.surface: Someone says it's a shame that you are staying celibate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shame' first suggests disgrace, which would suit the sexual surface, but it means pity here. UR for 'your' comes from text messages.
annotation.definitionFit: Purity can mean chastity, abstaining from sex.

entries.clue: School across street partner endorsed for the future (9)

indicatorNotes.across: POD stretches across ST + DATE, placing them between P-O and D

blocks.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
ST = street
your date is the partner you go out with

annotation.surface: A school on the other side of the road has a partner signing something for later.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is the misdirection: it is a group of whales, not a place of learning. A postdated cheque is signed with a date in the future.
annotation.definitionFit: A postdated cheque is endorsed with a later date, so it can only be cashed in the future.

entries.clue: Snubbed writer making a comeback to ridicule (3)

indicatorNotes.Snubbed: snub-nosed means short, so BIRO is cut short, giving BIR

blocks.note: a writer is a BIRO, a ballpoint pen; snubbed, it loses its end

annotation.surface: An author who was ignored returns and faces mockery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is not an author but a pen, the Biro. 'Snubbed' pretends to be social rejection; here it cuts the word short.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ribbing is the informal, good-natured end of ridicule.

entries.clue: Perhaps Clover left Rio unexpectedly (7)

indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the letters of LEFT RIO end up somewhere unexpected

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A woman named Clover suddenly left Rio de Janeiro.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Clover look like a person's name. It is the plant, and 'Perhaps' says clover is one example of a trefoil.
annotation.definitionFit: A trefoil is any plant with three-part leaves, clover being the classic example.

entries.clue: Essential, like class A drugs? (13)

blocks.note: straight definition
split the word after IN: these drugs are not something a chemist can dispense over the counter

annotation.surface: Someone claims hard drugs are necessary.
annotation.walkthrough: Class A is the most tightly controlled category of illegal drugs in the UK, such as heroin and LSD. The question mark flags the pun: they cannot be dispensed.
annotation.definitionFit: Indispensable means essential, impossible to do without.

entries.clue: A politician pursues enclosure to erect temporary accommodation (6)

indicatorNotes.pursues: A + MP follows, or pursues, ENC, so it comes after it

blocks.note: ENC is the standard abbreviation for an enclosure in a letter
used as is
MP = Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: A politician chases after a fenced-off area so they can put up a temporary shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' suggests a pen or paddock, but here it is the ENC written at the foot of a letter to show something is attached.
annotation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, with tents as temporary shelter.

entries.clue: Highly sought-after editor of plays (2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.plays: the letters of EDITOR OF play about and rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A much-wanted person edits theatre scripts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a noun, the dramas being edited; it is a verb telling the letters to move around.
annotation.definitionFit: Something 'to die for' is so desirable that people crave it.

entries.clue: Each authoritarian better finish off here in South African province (7,4)

indicatorNotes.finish off: the finish of 'here' is its last letter, E

blocks.note: EA = each, as on price tags
stern means strict and authoritarian
to cap a story is to better it
last letter of 'here'

annotation.surface: A strict gambler finishes up here, in a region of South Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective or a gambler; it is the verb 'to better', which is also 'to cap'.
annotation.definitionFit: Eastern Cape is one of South Africa's nine provinces.

entries.clue: One submitting main point in concerning angry outburst (10)

indicatorNotes.in: GIST goes in, between RE and RANT

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headings
the gist is the main point
a rant is an angry tirade

annotation.surface: Someone yielding gets the main point across in a furious tirade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Submitting' suggests surrender; here it means sending in your details. A registrant submits an application or registration.
annotation.definitionFit: A registrant is someone who submits their name or details to be registered.

entries.clue: I can act, primarily influencing troop manoeuvres? (9)

annotation.definition: I can act, primarily influencing troop manoeuvres?

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letters of 'influencing' and 'troop'
indicatorNotes.manoeuvres: the letters are manoeuvred into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
first letters of Influencing and Troop

annotation.surface: An officer boasts of their ability to direct soldiers' movements.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a tactician says 'I can act', mainly by steering troop manoeuvres.
annotation.definitionFit: A tactician plans military manoeuvres, directing how troops move in battle.

entries.clue: Identity cards ultimately being responsible for mischief (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of 'cards'

blocks.note: last letter of 'cards'
elves are the mischief-makers of folklore

annotation.surface: ID cards end up being the source of all the trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Identity cards' reads as ID documents, but the definition stops at 'Identity'.
annotation.definitionFit: Your self is your identity, the person you are.

entries.clue: Irritatingly complacent fools putting sons first (4)

indicatorNotes.putting sons first: the S that stands for sons moves from the end of MUGS to the front

blocks.note: S = son; it is the plural ending of MUGS, moved to the front
a mug is a gullible fool; MUGS without its final S

annotation.surface: Self-satisfied idiots put their boys ahead of everyone else.
annotation.walkthrough: The S already sits at the end of MUGS; the clue only asks you to move it to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Smug means annoyingly pleased with yourself.

entries.clue: Puts compost on church’s borders wearing shoes unsuitable for gardening (7)

indicatorNotes.borders: the borders of 'church' are its outer letters, C and H
indicatorNotes.wearing: CH is dressed in MULES, so it sits inside them

blocks.note: mules are backless slippers, no use in a flowerbed
first and last letters of 'church'

annotation.surface: A gardener in the wrong shoes spreads compost along the church flowerbeds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' pretends to be flowerbeds, which suits the gardening picture; it means the edges of the word 'church'.
annotation.definitionFit: To mulch is to spread compost or other material over soil.

entries.clue: Blur track covering Billie’s early recordings, primarily Strange Fruit? (10)

indicatorNotes.covering: CLOUD + RY covers BER, placing it between them
indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letters of Billie's, Early and Recordings

blocks.note: to cloud is to blur
first letters of Billie's Early Recordings
RY = railway, a track

annotation.surface: A song by the band Blur covers Billie Holiday's early recordings, especially Strange Fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: Blur is a British rock band, and Strange Fruit is Billie Holiday's 1939 song about lynching. The music is all misdirection: the answer is an unusual fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: The cloudberry is an amber berry from northern bogs, strange enough to most eaters.

entries.clue: Goods lost in transit away from home awhile (7)

blocks.note: if you are out, you are not at home
for ages = for a long while

annotation.surface: Parcels went missing on the way while their owner was away for a long time.
annotation.walkthrough: The usual sense of outage, a power cut, is not the one meant: an outage is also the quantity of goods lost in transport or storage.
annotation.definitionFit: Outage can mean the amount of goods lost or missing in transit or storage.

entries.clue: Go back again nurse (7)

blocks.note: to withdraw, as an army does
RE (again) + TREAT (nurse, care for a patient)

annotation.surface: A patient tells the nurse to go back again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a noun being addressed; it is a verb, to treat, and 'again' makes it re-treat.
annotation.definitionFit: Retreat means to go back or withdraw; re-treat means to treat again.

entries.clue: Fun composer announced collection of recordings (8)

indicatorNotes.announced: LISZT is spoken, not spelt, giving the sound LIST

blocks.note: play is fun and games
Franz Liszt, the Hungarian composer, is pronounced 'list'

annotation.surface: An entertaining composer is presented with a set of records.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fun composer' looks like a light-hearted musician, but it is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from radio and streaming: the chosen set of tracks to be played.

entries.clue: Bananas are not fancy! (6)

indicatorNotes.Bananas: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: Someone insists that bananas are not elegant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' reads as fruit, the subject of the sentence; in slang it means crazy, and that is what tells the letters to scramble.
annotation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is to say fancy.

entries.clue: Scouser’s audible disappointment with sibling’s band (5)

indicatorNotes.audible: the phrase is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a Liverpudlian letting out a let-down 'oh, eh' at their sister

annotation.surface: A Liverpudlian sighs over their brother's or sister's group.
annotation.walkthrough: A Scouser is someone from Liverpool. Oasis, the Manchester band, was famously run by two feuding brothers, Liam and Noel Gallagher, so 'sibling's band' suits them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Britpop group led by the Gallagher brothers is one band among many.

entries.clue: Troubled genius protected by landlord had somewhere to live (7,6)

indicatorNotes.Troubled: GENIUS is troubled, its letters stirred up
indicatorNotes.protected by: the anagram is sheltered inside HOST

blocks.note: a landlord, especially of a pub, is the host
anagram of GENIUS, placed inside HO-ST
had dinner = ate dinner

annotation.surface: A tormented genius, sheltered by their landlord, had a place to stay.
annotation.walkthrough: A housing estate is a British term for a planned area of homes, often council-built.
annotation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned development of homes, somewhere people live.

entries.clue: Regularly take public transport naked (3)

indicatorNotes.naked: BUSES is stripped of its outer layer, its first and last letters

blocks.note: BUSES without B and S

annotation.surface: Someone rides the bus every day without any clothes on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' pretends to be an alternate-letters signal, which would give EUA or AE; it is part of the definition, as in using a drug regularly.
annotation.definitionFit: A drug-world sense: a habitual taker is a user, so the verb carries the 'regularly'.

entries.clue: Headmaster noticed lagging behind (6)

indicatorNotes.lagging: lagging is insulating wrap, so 'Headmaster noticed' wraps around the answer

blocks.note: headmASTER Noticed

annotation.surface: The head teacher spotted a pupil falling behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lagging behind' reads as one phrase about a slow pupil; split it, and 'lagging' wraps the hidden letters while 'behind' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Astern means behind, towards the back of a ship.

entries.clue: Has a feeling American president’s beginning to divide factions (8)

indicatorNotes.to divide: US + P splits SECTS, sitting between S and ECTS

blocks.note: sects are factions or splinter groups; US + P goes after the first S
US = American
first letter of 'president'

annotation.surface: Someone senses a US president is starting to split the country into factions.
annotation.walkthrough: The political picture works so well that 'American president' reads as one person; it is US plus P.
annotation.definitionFit: If someone suspects something, they have a feeling it is true.
